reanchored_why: THE KEYS MOVED BECAUSE THE BLOCK BOUNDARY MOVED, NOT BECAUSE THE CORPUS CHANGED. The detector was split at and stripped tags before testing for an anchor, so a citation table read as unanchored: the title sat in one cell, its PubMed link in the cell beside it, and the link's URL lived in an href attribute that was deleted before the anchor test ran. Segmentation is now per and hrefs are tested. A key is block[:70], so a block that grew a leading header cell re-keys without changing. RE-ANCHORING A RATCHET IS THE MOVE MOST EASILY USED TO LAUNDER A CLEARANCE, so every key that left is accounted for individually below and the pairing was done on the FULL block text, not on the truncated key.

one_frozen_key_split_into_two.what: THREE blocks on this page opened with the same 70 characters, so ONE frozen key stood for all three. Merging cells into rows gave one of them a leading header cell, so it now keys separately. The page did not change and no finding was added -- a key that was doing the work of three is now doing the work of two. This is the failure mode of keying on a text WINDOW rather than on content, and it is recorded here because it is indistinguishable, from the count alone, from a new defect.
